title: Rapid DNA Act of 2017
official_summary:
(This measure has not been amended since it was introduced. The expanded summary of the House reported version is repeated here.)

Rapid DNA Act of 2017

(Sec. 2) This bill amends the DNA Identification Act of 1994 to require the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) to issue standards and procedures for using Rapid DNA instruments to analyze DNA samples of criminal offenders.

Rapid DNA instruments carry out a fully automated process to create a DNA analysis from a DNA sample.

DNA samples prepared by criminal justice agencies using Rapid DNA instruments in compliance the FBI-issued standards and procedures may be included in the Combined DNA Index System (CODIS).

(Sec. 3) The bill amends the DNA Analysis Backlog Elimination Act of 2000 to allow the FBI to waive certain existing requirements if a DNA sample is analyzed using Rapid DNA instruments and the results are included in CODIS.

summary.headline: This 2017 law lets police and criminal justice agencies use fast, fully automated DNA testing machines, with FBI standards, and add those results to the national DNA database.
summary.what_it_does: The law requires the FBI to create standards and procedures for using Rapid DNA instruments, which are machines that automatically turn a DNA sample into a DNA analysis. DNA samples prepared by criminal justice agencies using these machines, and following FBI standards, can be included in the Combined DNA Index System (CODIS), the national DNA database. The law also lets the FBI waive certain existing requirements when a sample is analyzed with Rapid DNA and the results are added to CODIS.

who_it_affects.group: Criminal justice agencies such as police and crime labs
who_it_affects.how: They can use Rapid DNA machines to analyze samples and add results to CODIS if they follow FBI standards and procedures.
It must issue standards and procedures for Rapid DNA use and may waive some existing DNA analysis requirements for samples run on these machines.

who_it_affects.group: People who have been convicted of crimes and whose DNA is collected
who_it_affects.how: Their DNA samples may be processed with Rapid DNA machines and entered into CODIS under the new rules.
